title: Rust verify_chain has no depth cap — WASM stack overflow on deep chains
rationale: Added const MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH: usize = 16; (mirroring Go layer's maxChainDepth=16 in chain.go:43) and guard after EMPTY_CHAIN check in verify_chain. Returns CHAIN_TOO_DEEP with matching error code, message format, and suggestion string before any JWT decoding or crypto work.
variants_checked: chain/verify.rs:verify_chain — no depth guard existed; wasm/bindings.rs:wasm_verify_chain — calls verify_chain directly (the WASM surface), now protected
bypass_considered: WASM caller passes 17-receipt bundle: depth check at receipts.len()>16 fires before any heap allocation for decoded-receipt vector
test_note: chain_depth_over_limit_is_rejected (17 stub receipts → CHAIN_TOO_DEEP) and chain_depth_at_limit_is_not_depth_rejected (16 receipts → not CHAIN_TOO_DEEP) added to test_verify_chain.rs
review_reason: Both hunks squarely on the verify_chain call path — constant and guard in the flagged function, test file directly exercises it. Patch fixes root cause by bounding input before any crypto or allocation work begins, mirroring the already-deployed maxChainDepth=16 in drs-verify/pkg/verify/chain.go:43. No new parsing, no new trust surface, no existing security check weakened.
